docs.title: MeerKAT Long-Period Transients
docs.text:
Monitoring long-period radio transients with MeerKAT (project SCI-20251201-ID-01).

Long-period radio transients (LPTs) are Galactic radio sources that emit bright, highly polarised pulses with periods of minutes to hours, much longer than ordinary radio pulsars. Several have been shown to be white dwarfs in binaries with M-dwarf companions, while the nature of others is still open. This project uses regular MeerKAT observations to follow how their pulses, brightness and polarisation change over time.

docs.title: How the TOAs were measured
docs.text:
• Data: dynamic spectra made from the MeerKAT visibilities at the source position (UHF band), at 8 s time resolution.
  • TOA: the centre of a Gaussian fitted to the band-averaged Stokes I light curve. When pulses overlap, they are fitted together. The error is the 1σ uncertainty on the fitted centre.
  • Time system: topocentric UTC at MeerKAT. The TOAs are not barycentred and not corrected for dispersion. In the .tim files the site code is meerkat and the frequency is the band centre (816 MHz).
  • Multiple pulses: observations with more than one pulse, or a pulse with several components, have one TOA per component.
